This 'West Side Story' revival at the Palace Theatre is a thrilling testament to the musical'
‘West Side Story’ blasts back to Broadway — kinetic, bloody and modern to the core

In the production that opened Thursday night at the Palace Theater, which lovingly replicates Mr. Robbins’s balletic choreography, what prevails is a tenderhearted awareness of the naked vulnerability of being young and trapped in an urban jungle.
But this revival is a coup for the director Arthur Laurents, who at 91-years-old delivers a radically different perspective on the play he wrote more than 50 years ago.
There’s nothing dated about Arthur Laurents’ striking revival of his West Side Story which first opened on Broadway in 1957.

cn.t: This revival earns praise for its enduring power and Laurents's bold bilingual approach, though some find the production's sweetness undercuts the musical's edge. Critics largely celebrate the timeless choreography and emotional depth.

vs.sum: Spectacularly renovated in a $100M+ project that literally raised the theater 30 feet. The restoration preserved its opulent 1913 interior while upgrading acoustics, seating comfort, and best-in-class restrooms on every level — widely considered the best facilities on Broadway.

acc.note: Elevator to all levels. Wheelchair, aisle transfer, and companion seating on all levels.
